title: DOJ to form panel to vet Truth Commission findings on drug war killings
summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) will form a fact-finding panel to review the Truth Commission's report on drug war killings under the Duterte administration, following the presentation of the…

blocks.text: The Department of Justice (DOJ) will form a fact-finding panel to review the Truth Commission's report on drug war killings under the Duterte administration, following the presentation of the commission's preliminary findings.

Speaking at the Truth Commission's national conference on Monday, Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida said the DOJ would need to thoroughly examine the evidence gathered by the commission to ensure that any charges eventually filed in court would be strong enough to withstand legal scrutiny.

"Yes, definitely we will have a panel to review everything because we will check on the verifiable facts. What are the pieces of evidence? Are they purely testimonial? Are they purely physical evidence?” Vida said.
“The whole gamut, the whole spectrum, right? Because we don't want to file weak cases if ever they will be filed,” he added.
During the conference, former International Criminal Court (ICC) judge and current Truth Commission chairperson Raul Pangalangan presented the group's initial findings.

While emphasizing that the report was still preliminary, the commission said the evidence gathered was already sufficient to conclude that the drug war killings under former President Rodrigo Duterte were “state-organized.”
It also said the government's “official account cannot be accepted at face value” and that, in cases brought forward by victims' families, “no one has been held to account.”
The Truth Commission also presented the following key findings:

items: 8,320 documented killings, a figure expected to increase
Victims were overwhelmingly men of working and parenting age
Killings were concentrated in urban communities
Operations began almost everywhere at once and followed the police
Many killings bore the marks of execution
The official “manlaban” account did not hold up
Official records were incomplete and at times unreliable
Families had effectively carried out the State's investigative work
The drug war did not end in 2022
The commission proposed 27 reforms, five of which it said could not wait

blocks.text: The DOJ acknowledged that building cases from the available evidence would be challenging, particularly in establishing the credibility and admissibility of accounts provided by victims' families.
“Yes, very challenging, kasi yung sinabi nila kanina eh di ba kapag victim, totoo naman to eh, ‘Sabi kasi nung ano nakaluhod na yung anak ko nung binaril.’ Sabi nga nila. Di ba hearsay?” Vida said.
(Yes, very challenging, because, as mentioned earlier, a family member might say, ‘Someone told me my child was already kneeling when he was shot.’ Isn't that hearsay?)
"Who was actually there when it happened? These are the challenges in conducting the investigation and building up a case," he added.
Duterte is currently detained at the ICC detention facility in The Hague, with his trial proper for crimes against humanity scheduled to begin on November 30.
Vida said he was not in favor of holding local proceedings simultaneously with the ICC trial, stressing that the DOJ must first determine the appropriate legal strategy.

“I don't like simultaneous proceedings. That's different, right? Because you're running into the possibility of a conflict. It could be complementary, or it could involve sequencing. It depends on the proper and appropriate legal strategy,” he said.
The Justice secretary said the department remained committed to fulfilling its mandate “for the people and by the people.”— MCG, GMA News
